themes.name: CNN Architecture Benchmarking on Fashion-MNIST
themes.description: A large body of work systematically evaluates CNN architectures of varying depth and complexity on Fashion-MNIST, establishing performance baselines. Studies range from simple two-block CNNs achieving ~88–90% accuracy to optimized residual networks reaching 96%+. These provide important context for interpreting results from a small CNN.

themes.name: Effect of Data Augmentation on CNN Generalization
themes.description: Several studies directly measure how standard geometric augmentations (flips, rotations, translations, shifts) affect CNN classification accuracy and overfitting. The consistent finding is that augmentation improves generalization, particularly for small datasets or short training runs, though the magnitude varies by architecture and domain.

themes.name: Advanced and Adaptive Augmentation Strategies
themes.description: A distinct research thread moves beyond basic geometric transforms toward class-conditional, policy-optimized, or generative augmentation methods. These approaches (WeMix, MFG Augment, LMix, class-adaptive policies, VAEs) seek to correct distribution shift introduced by augmentation or adapt transforms per class, and consistently outperform naive augmentation on standard benchmarks.

themes.name: Hyperparameter and Regularization Tuning on Fashion-MNIST
themes.description: Multiple studies treat Fashion-MNIST as a testbed for examining the interaction between hyperparameters (filter size, batch size, dropout rate, learning rate, normalization placement) and model accuracy. These papers highlight that architecture choices and regularization can dominate augmentation effects, complicating isolated analysis.

themes.name: Transfer Learning and Lightweight CNNs
themes.description: A pragmatic thread addresses deployment constraints by building efficient lightweight CNNs or fine-tuning pre-trained models, often combining augmentation with transfer learning. These studies show that augmentation's benefit is architecture- and data-scale-dependent, and diminishes when pre-trained representations are available.

themes.name: Quantum and Hybrid CNN Architectures
themes.description: An emerging niche applies quantum computing concepts to CNN design on Fashion-MNIST, replacing classical convolutional filters with quantum circuits. While parameter-efficient, these approaches currently underperform classical CNNs on complex tasks and remain limited by hardware constraints.

overview.summary:
The use of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image classification on Fashion-MNIST is a well-established benchmark, with dozens of studies reporting accuracies ranging from roughly 88% for simple architectures up to ~99.65% for heavily optimized models. Data augmentation — including basic geometric transforms like flips, rotations, and translations — is widely recognized as a practical regularization tool that reduces overfitting and improves generalization, especially in low-data or short-training regimes.

Despite the abundance of Fashion-MNIST studies, clean controlled comparisons isolating the effect of basic augmentation on a small CNN are surprisingly rare: most papers either apply augmentation as one component in a larger optimization pipeline, or omit it entirely. The field has matured toward increasingly complex architectures and augmentation strategies (Mixup, CutOut, AutoAugment), which makes the proposed study's focused, reproducible, seed-controlled design a useful empirical baseline contribution.
open_problems: Isolating the contribution of basic augmentation from other simultaneously varied factors (architecture depth, regularization, optimizer) remains rare in the literature
Most Fashion-MNIST studies do not report results across multiple fixed random seeds, making it hard to distinguish genuine improvement from seed-dependent variance
The regime in which simple augmentation (flip/rotation/translation) actually helps small CNNs vs. larger or pre-trained models is not well characterized
Short training runs (~5 epochs) may not give augmentation enough time to reduce overfitting, and optimal epoch count for observing augmentation benefit is underexplored
Fashion-MNIST accuracy gains from augmentation appear modest (~1–2%) in short runs, raising the question of whether improvements are practically meaningful given measurement noise
The interaction between augmentation strength (degree of rotation/translation) and dataset difficulty has not been systematically studied on Fashion-MNIST
Reproducibility is inconsistently ensured: many papers omit random seed details, preventing direct comparison of results across studies

papers.title: Hyperparameter Optimization and Regularization on Fashion-MNIST Classification
papers.venue: International Journal of Recent Technology and Engineering (IJRTE)

notes.problem: How do hyperparameter optimization methods and regularization techniques affect CNN performance on the Fashion-MNIST benchmark?
limitations: No comparison with state-of-the-art results reported with specific numbers
Limited to a single dataset
notes.contribution: Explores hyperparameter optimization and regularization techniques for CNN-based image classification on Fashion-MNIST with data augmentation.
key_findings: Proposed deep ConvNet architectures with data augmentation achieve impressive results on Fashion-MNIST
Data augmentation techniques such as cropping, rotation, flipping, and shifting help address insufficient training samples

papers.title: CNN Model for Image Classification on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST Dataset

notes.problem: How do CNN architecture choices and hyperparameters affect image classification accuracy on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST?
limitations: Limited to two benchmark datasets
No comparison with non-CNN baselines
notes.contribution: Systematic evaluation of five CNN architectures with varying hyperparameters for image classification on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST
key_findings: All five architectures achieve >99% accuracy on MNIST
Architecture 3 gives best results on Fashion-MNIST
Activation function, optimizer, and dropout rate have the most impact on accuracy

papers.title: State-of-the-Art Results with the Fashion-MNIST Dataset

notes.problem: How well can classical ML models and simple CNNs classify Fashion-MNIST images, and how does the number of trainable parameters affect classification quality?
limitations: Experiments limited to Fashion-MNIST; generalizability to other datasets not demonstrated
notes.contribution: A CNN with three convolutional layers (CNN-3-128) achieves 99.65% accuracy on Fashion-MNIST, setting a new state-of-the-art result.
key_findings: CNN-3-128 achieved 99.65% accuracy on the Fashion-MNIST test set
There is a dependence between the number of adjustable parameters in a CNN and the maximum achievable classification quality

papers.title: CNN-Based Image Classification on the Fashion-MNIST Dataset
papers.venue: International Journal of Emerging Multidisciplinaries Computer Science & Artificial Intelligence
authors: Abdul Salam Shah Sayed Chia Chen Yee

notes.problem: How well does a standard CNN architecture classify grayscale fashion images across ten categories with high intra- and inter-class visual similarity?
limitations: Single relatively simple architecture evaluated
No data augmentation applied
Attention-based or more complex architectures not explored
notes.contribution: Empirical evaluation of a sequential CNN for multi-class image classification on Fashion-MNIST achieving 88.85% test accuracy
key_findings: Achieved 88.85% test accuracy with no major overfitting
Morphologically distinctive categories (trousers, bags, footwear) showed high discriminative performance
Systematic inter-class confusion observed among upper-body garments (shirts, T-shirts, pullovers)

papers.title: Convolutional Neural Networks and Vision Transformers for Fashion MNIST Classification: A Literature Review

notes.problem: Which architecture, CNN or ViT, is more appropriate for classifying Fashion MNIST images in e-commerce, and how do their combinations perform?
limitations: No new experiments conducted; conclusions are based solely on existing literature
notes.contribution: A literature review comparing CNNs and Vision Transformers for clothing image classification on Fashion MNIST, identifying factors influencing performance and the potential of hybrid architectures.
key_findings: CNNs excel at recognizing local patterns while ViTs are effective at capturing global context
Combining CNNs and ViTs can leverage their complementary strengths for improved classification performance
Performance is influenced by dataset characteristics, image dimensions, number of target classes, and hardware infrastructure

papers.title: РЕЗУЛЬТАТИ НАЛАШТУВАННЯ ПАРАМЕТРІВ НЕЙРОННИХ ГЛИБОКИХ МЕРЕЖ ЩОДО РОЗПІЗНАВАННЯ FASHION MNIST DATASET

notes.problem: How do CNN architecture choices and training parameters affect recognition accuracy on the Fashion-MNIST dataset?
limitations: Only 20 training epochs used
Limited to two selected sequential CNN architectures
notes.contribution: Empirical study of CNN hyperparameter tuning (batch_size, BatchNormalization placement, filters, validation strategy, Dropout) to improve Fashion-MNIST recognition accuracy up to 94.16%
key_findings: Achieved 94.16% recognition accuracy on Fashion-MNIST with an optimized CNN architecture
Using test data as validation set (valid_data) instead of validation_split improved accuracy by increasing effective training data
batch_size and Dropout layer tuning significantly influenced recognition accuracy and overfitting

papers.title: Revolutionizing Digit Image Recognition: Pushing the Limits with Simple CNN and Challenging Image Augmentation Techniques on MNIST

notes.problem: How can image augmentation techniques improve CNN-based handwritten digit recognition accuracy?
limitations: Evaluated only on MNIST; more challenging datasets not explored
CNN architecture improvements not investigated in this work
notes.contribution: Applies CNN with image augmentation techniques to achieve 99.81% accuracy on MNIST digit recognition.
key_findings: CNN with image augmentation achieved maximum accuracy of 99.81% on MNIST
Ensemble of CNN models achieved 99.79% accuracy
Image augmentation techniques effectively reduced overfitting and improved performance

papers.title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Image Classification
papers.venue: International Journal of Emerging Multidisciplinaries Computer Science & Artificial Intelligence
authors: Abdul Salam Shah Sayed Gam Chui Ern

notes.problem: How can CNN-based image classification be applied to Fashion-MNIST and extended to real-world textile sorting for circular economy purposes?
limitations: Confusion among visually similar garment categories limits performance
Extension to real industrial systems relies on cited third-party pilot results rather than original experiments
notes.contribution: A regularized CNN achieving ~90% accuracy on Fashion-MNIST is presented and its application to sustainable fashion/textile circular economy systems is outlined.
key_findings: Model achieves ~90% test accuracy on the 10,000-sample Fashion-MNIST test set
High F1 scores for morphologically distinct categories (Trouser, Bag, Sandal: F1≥0.97) but lower for visually similar garments (Shirt: F1≈0.74)
CNN-based classifiers report 93% accuracy in intelligent textile sorting pilots and 95% accuracy in post-consumer fabric recycling pipelines at one item/second

papers.title: Enhancing Image Classification with Augmentation: Data Augmentation Techniques for Improved Image Classification

notes.problem: CNNs overfit on small datasets, and it is unclear which data augmentation techniques best mitigate this problem.
limitations: Evaluation limited to a single dataset (Caltech-101)
Only one base model (EfficientNet-B0) used for comparison
notes.contribution: Proposes three novel data augmentation techniques (pairwise channel transfer, object occlusion, novel masking) and evaluates 11 augmentation sets for improved image classification with CNNs.
key_findings: An ensemble of diverse augmentation techniques achieves the best performance on Caltech-101.
The three novel augmentation techniques (channel transfer, object occlusion, masking) contribute to improved classification accuracy.
Diverse data augmentation is a viable means of enhancing small datasets to reduce overfitting.

papers.title: Information Bottleneck Theory on Convolutional Neural Networks

notes.problem: How does Information Bottleneck theory explain the dynamic training behavior of convolutional neural networks?
limitations: Experiments limited to MNIST and Fashion-MNIST datasets.
notes.contribution: Applies Information Bottleneck theory to analyze the training dynamics of CNNs and investigates how architectural features affect IB behavior.
key_findings: The compression phase predicted by IB theory is not observed in CNNs in all tested cases.
CNNs exhibit more complicated behavior than feedforward neural networks under IB theory.

papers.title: Classification of Garments from Fashion MNIST Dataset Using CNN LeNet-5 Architecture
papers.venue: 2020 International Conference on Innovative Trends in Communication and Computer Engineering (ITCE)

notes.problem: Classifying clothing items from images is challenging due to high inter-class similarity and complex category depth
notes.contribution: Applies LeNet-5 CNN architecture to Fashion MNIST garment classification, achieving over 98% accuracy
key_findings: LeNet-5 achieved over 98% accuracy on Fashion MNIST
LeNet-5 outperformed classical CNN and other state-of-the-art models in the literature

papers.title: Classification of fashion article images using convolutional neural networks
papers.venue: International Conference on Image Information Processing (ICIIP)

notes.problem: How to accurately classify fashion article images using deep learning.
notes.contribution: Three CNN architectures with batch normalization and residual skip connections achieving ~2% accuracy improvement on Fashion-MNIST classification.
key_findings: Proposed CNN models achieve ~2% accuracy improvement over existing state-of-the-art on Fashion-MNIST.

papers.title: Remote sensing image scene classification using CNN-MLP with data augmentation

notes.problem: How to improve VHR remote sensing image scene classification by better capturing object relationships within images.
limitations: Evaluated only on three datasets
Limited discussion of computational cost
notes.contribution: A CNN-MLP model combining pre-trained CNN feature extraction with an Adagrad-optimized MLP classifier and data augmentation for remote sensing scene classification.
key_findings: CNN-MLP outperforms state-of-the-art methods on UC-Merced, AID, and NWPU-RESISC45 datasets
Using MLP with Adagrad optimizer as a deep classifier improves upon standard CNN fully connected layers
Data augmentation helps mitigate limited training samples per class

papers.title: Deep CNN and Data Augmentation for Skin Lesion Classification
papers.venue: Asian Conference on Intelligent Information and Database Systems

notes.problem: How to improve skin lesion classification performance under limited data conditions.
notes.contribution: A deep CNN model with data augmentation for improved skin lesion classification.
key_findings: Data augmentation helps overcome data limitation and improves skin lesion classification performance with deep CNN.

papers.title: Rectified Exponential Units for Convolutional Neural Networks

notes.problem: How to design an activation function that improves upon ReLU and other variants in convolutional neural networks.
notes.contribution: Proposes Rectified Exponential Unit (REU) and its parametric variant (PREU) as novel activation functions for CNNs that combine flexible exponent and multiplicative form.
key_findings: REU achieves relative error improvements over ReLU of 7.74% and 6.08% on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with ResNet
PREU achieves relative error improvements of 9.24% and 9.32% on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with ResNet

papers.title: Effect of filter sizes on image classification in CNN: a case study on CFIR10 and Fashion-MNIST datasets
papers.venue: IAES International Journal of Artificial Intelligence (IJ-AI)

notes.problem: How does CNN filter size affect image classification accuracy?
limitations: Only three filter sizes tested
Single architecture evaluated
notes.contribution: Empirical study showing how varying CNN filter sizes (3×3, 5×5, 7×7) affects image classification accuracy on CIFAR-10 and Fashion-MNIST.
key_findings: Accuracy is inversely proportional to filter size
3×3 filters achieved 73.04% accuracy on CIFAR-10 and 93.68% on Fashion-MNIST

papers.title: Class-Adaptive Data Augmentation for Image Classification

notes.problem: How to find appropriate data augmentation policies that vary per class to better reflect class-specific characteristics in image classification.
limitations: Requires an initial training phase without augmentation before deriving policies, increasing overall training cost.
Evaluated primarily on benchmark datasets; generalization to more diverse real-world datasets is unclear.
notes.contribution: A class-adaptive data augmentation method that derives class-specific augmentation policies by maximizing transformation degree while preserving label consistency in CNNs.
key_findings: Class-specific augmentation policies achieve comparable or higher classification accuracy than uniform augmentation baselines.
Derived class-specific policies are consistent with domain knowledge of each dataset.

papers.title: Effect of data-augmentation on fine-tuned CNN model performance
papers.venue: IAES International Journal of Artificial Intelligence (IJ-AI)

notes.problem: How does data augmentation affect the performance of fine-tuned CNN models when training data is limited?
limitations: Custom dataset limited to binary classification (cats vs dogs)
Results may not generalize to other domains or larger datasets
notes.contribution: Empirical analysis showing data augmentation improves fine-tuned CNN (VGG16, ResNet50) classification performance on a cats vs. dogs dataset
key_findings: ResNet50 with data augmentation achieved 90% test accuracy vs 82% without data augmentation
Both VGG16 and ResNet50 achieved better test accuracy when data augmentation was employed
ResNet50 outperformed VGG16 in all experimental conditions

papers.title: Classification of Fashion-MNIST Dataset by Using Lenet-5
papers.venue: Science and Technology of Engineering Chemistry and Environmental Protection

notes.problem: How effective is the classic LeNet-5 architecture on the Fashion-MNIST dataset for clothing image classification?
limitations: Only one model (LeNet-5) evaluated without comparison to more modern architectures
notes.contribution: Applies LeNet-5 CNN to Fashion-MNIST image classification and evaluates its effectiveness as a benchmark task.
key_findings: LeNet-5 achieves 95% training accuracy on Fashion-MNIST
LeNet-5 achieves 90% validation accuracy, indicating good generalization

papers.title: An Analysis of Convolutional Neural Network for Fashion Images Classification (Fashion-MNIST)
papers.venue: Advances in Intelligent Systems and Computing

notes.problem: How to improve CNN performance for fashion image classification using Fashion-MNIST?
notes.contribution: Proposes a simple CNN architecture modification to improve and accelerate learning on Fashion-MNIST classification.
key_findings: Proposed modification to CNN architecture improves and accelerates the learning process on Fashion-MNIST.

papers.title: Classification of Standard FASHION MNIST Dataset Using Deep Learning Based CNN Algorithms
papers.venue: International Symposium on Multidisciplinary Studies and Innovative Technologies (ISMSIT)

notes.problem: How to improve CNN-based image classification on Fashion MNIST while mitigating model overfitting.
limitations: Only two custom architectures compared; no benchmark against well-known models like ResNet or VGG
notes.contribution: Two CNN architectures (CNN-C1 and CNN-C2) are proposed and compared for Fashion MNIST image classification, with CNN-C2 achieving 93.11% accuracy.
key_findings: CNN-C2 outperforms CNN-C1 and achieves 93.11% accuracy on Fashion MNIST

papers.title: Classifying Garments from Fashion-MNIST Dataset Through CNNs

notes.problem: How to accurately classify garment images from the Fashion-MNIST dataset using CNNs.
notes.contribution: Four CNN models for Fashion-MNIST garment classification achieving 99.1% accuracy, outperforming prior best of 89.7% with SVM.
key_findings: Best CNN model (cnn-dropout-3) achieved 99.1% accuracy, improving over the 89.7% SVM baseline from the original Fashion-MNIST paper.

papers.title: Circular Shift: An Effective Data Augmentation Method For Convolutional Neural Network On Image Classification

notes.problem: Common augmentation methods like rotation, crop, and flip can degrade performance for small images or objects with dispersed features.
limitations: Evaluated only on small image datasets
No theoretical analysis of why circular shift outperforms other augmentations
notes.contribution: A circular shift data augmentation method for CNNs that shifts images cyclically to provide variation without losing information.
key_findings: Circular shift augmentation consistently improves classification performance across different CNN-based models
Circular shift can be combined with existing augmentation methods for further performance gains
Circular shift avoids information loss that can occur with crop or rotation on small images

papers.title: Understanding how noise affects the accuracy of CNN image classification
papers.venue: Journal of Applied Technology and Innovation

notes.problem: How does the presence or absence of noise augmentation affect CNN image classification accuracy?
limitations: Abstract does not specify datasets used
No numerical results reported in abstract
notes.contribution: Empirical evaluation of how noise augmentation affects CNN image classification accuracy in training and testing
key_findings: Noise augmentation affects CNN classification accuracy in both training and testing phases

papers.title: Using Ultrasound Image Augmentation and Ensemble Predictions to Prevent Machine-Learning Model Overfitting

notes.problem: How to improve generalization of deep learning ultrasound image classifiers when training data is limited and subject variability is high.
limitations: Evaluated only on tissue phantoms, not clinical subjects
Limited dataset size necessitating augmentation
notes.contribution: Demonstrates that image augmentation and ensemble (bagging) predictions reduce overfitting and improve ultrasound shrapnel classification accuracy from <70% to >85%.
key_findings: Baseline LOSO test accuracy was <70% and variable
Affine augmentation or MixUp improved accuracy to ~75%
Top-3 LOSO confidence bagging improved accuracy to >85% on two blind tissue phantoms

papers.title: WeMix: How to Better Utilize Data Augmentation

notes.problem: Conventional data augmentation creates a biased data distribution that leads to suboptimal model performance.
limitations: Evaluation datasets not specified in abstract
notes.contribution: WeMix combines AugDrop and MixLoss to correct data bias introduced by data augmentation, improving generalization.
key_findings: Data augmentation introduces data bias where augmented distribution differs from original distribution
AugDrop and MixLoss each theoretically guarantee bias correction and improve data augmentation
WeMix combining both algorithms shows consistent empirical improvements over standard augmentation

papers.title: ROTATION-GAMMA CORRECTION AUGMENTATION ON CNN-DENSE BLOCK FOR SOIL IMAGE CLASSIFICATION

notes.problem: How to accurately classify soil images by color with limited training data while addressing vanishing/exploding gradient problems in CNNs.
limitations: Classification is not based on standard soil taxonomy (e.g., Entisols, Histosols) but on arbitrary color-based categories
Small original dataset of only 156 images
notes.contribution: A rotation-gamma correction augmentation combined with a CNN-Dense block architecture for soil image classification by color achieving above 90% on all metrics.
key_findings: Augmentation increased training data from 156 to 2500 images
All performance metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score) exceeded 90%
CNN-Dense block with rotation-gamma correction augmentation is robust for color-based soil classification

papers.title: A novel CNN+LSTM classification model based on fashion-MNIST
papers.venue: Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering

notes.problem: How to improve image classification accuracy on the Fashion-MNIST dataset by combining CNN and LSTM architectures
limitations: 91.36% accuracy acknowledged as still needing improvement
notes.contribution: A hybrid CNN+LSTM model for image classification on Fashion-MNIST achieving 91.36% accuracy
key_findings: The CNN+LSTM hybrid model achieves 91.36% classification accuracy on Fashion-MNIST, outperforming compared baseline models

papers.title: Evaluating unified training optimisations for MobileNetV2: Efficiency-accuracy trade-offs in fine-grained dog breed classification

notes.problem: How to efficiently train MobileNetV2 for fine-grained classification under small-data and resource-constrained settings without significant accuracy loss.
limitations: Evaluated on a small subset of Stanford Dogs (1290 images, 8 breeds), limiting generalisability.
Results may not generalise to other fine-grained or large-scale datasets.
notes.contribution: A unified training optimisation pipeline for MobileNetV2 combining transfer learning, dynamic augmentation, dropout, adaptive LR scheduling, and early stopping that reduces training time by 50–70% with only 1.4% accuracy drop on fine-grained dog breed classification.
key_findings: Optimised pipeline reduces training time by 50–70% (609 s vs. 1213 s) and inference latency by 10% (0.028 s vs. 0.031 s per image) with only 1.4% accuracy drop (98.6% vs. 100.0%).
Statistical tests confirm significant efficiency gains (p < 0.001) and marginal accuracy loss (p = 0.0008).
MobileNetV2 with the optimised pipeline outperforms MobileNetV3Small and EfficientNetB0 under identical small-data conditions.

papers.title: Optimal Design of Deep Residual Network Based on Image Classification of Fashion-MNIST Dataset

notes.problem: How to design an optimal deep residual network architecture and training process for Fashion-MNIST classification.
limitations: Study limited to Fashion-MNIST dataset
Hyper-parameter search scope not fully specified
notes.contribution: An optimized deep residual network design achieving 96.21% accuracy on Fashion-MNIST image classification.
key_findings: Optimal model achieved 96.21% accuracy on Fashion-MNIST
Widening the network and using advanced training processes improves model performance

papers.title: Empirical Evaluation of the Effectiveness of Variational Autoencoders on Data Augmentation for the Image Classification Problem
papers.venue: International Journal of Intelligent Systems and Applications in Engineering

notes.problem: Whether variational autoencoders can effectively augment training data to improve image classification performance
limitations: Only one generative model (VAE) evaluated
Only one dataset (CIFAR-10) used
notes.contribution: Empirical evaluation of VAE-based data augmentation compared to transformation-based methods for image classification
key_findings: VAE augmentation is as effective as transformation-based augmentation methods
The contribution of data augmentation is sensitive to the size of the dataset

papers.title: Dysgraphia Handwriting Image Augmentation for CNN Model Classification
papers.venue: IEEE International Conference on Control System, Computing and Engineering

notes.problem: How to improve CNN classification of dysgraphia handwriting when large labeled datasets are scarce.
limitations: Small original dataset requiring augmentation
Only rotation and brightness augmentation techniques explored
No intelligence-based augmentation implemented yet
notes.contribution: A CNN-based dysgraphia handwriting classification model using rotation and brightness augmentation to address limited training data.
key_findings: Augmented data achieved 77% accuracy compared to 73% without augmentation, a 4% improvement.
Rotation and brightness augmentation significantly improved CNN classification of four dysgraphia handwriting classes.

papers.title: Fashion-MNIST Classification Based on CNN Image Recognition
papers.venue: Highlights in Science Engineering and Technology

notes.problem: Which classic CNN architecture achieves the highest classification accuracy on Fashion-MNIST with limited training samples?
limitations: Small dataset of 70,000 images limits generalizability
Only three CNN architectures compared
notes.contribution: Empirical comparison of DenseNet121, MobileNet, and ResNet50 on Fashion-MNIST image classification, finding DenseNet121 most accurate.
key_findings: DenseNet121 outperforms MobileNet and ResNet50 on Fashion-MNIST under controlled training conditions

papers.title: A Multi-Scale Convolutional Neural Network for Rotation-Invariant Recognition

notes.problem: How to effectively recognize rotated objects in images without relying solely on data augmentation.
limitations: Only considers D4 (90-degree) rotations, not arbitrary angle rotations
notes.contribution: Proposes RIMS-CNN, a multi-scale CNN with dihedral group D4 equivariance for rotation-invariant image recognition.
key_findings: RIMS-CNN achieves significant improvements over baseline models on all four benchmark datasets
Learning inherent convolution kernels for rotational features outperforms data augmentation with randomly rotated images

papers.title: Class-Conditional Data Augmentation Applied to Image Classification
papers.venue: International Conference on Computer Analysis of Images and Patterns

notes.problem: How to improve image classification robustness and reduce model uncertainty through data augmentation.
notes.contribution: A class-conditional data augmentation procedure that improves classification robustness and reduces epistemic uncertainty.
key_findings: Class-conditional data augmentation improves classification results and reduces epistemic uncertainty.

papers.title: Building Efficient Lightweight CNN Models

notes.problem: How to build CNNs that maintain competitive accuracy while meeting the computational and memory constraints of resource-limited environments.
limitations: Lower performance on complex datasets like CIFAR-10
Methodology evaluated only on classification tasks
Architectural scalability for more complex datasets needs further improvement
notes.contribution: A two-stage training methodology combining dual-input-output models and transfer learning with progressive unfreezing to build lightweight CNNs with competitive accuracy.
key_findings: Achieved 99% accuracy on MNIST and 89% on Fashion-MNIST with only 14,862 parameters and 0.17 MB model size.
CIFAR-10 accuracy was 65% with fewer than 20,000 parameters, showing scalability limits on complex datasets.
Progressive unfreezing enabled faster convergence and improved accuracy during fine-tuning.

papers.title: Robustness of Convolutional Neural Networks to Partial Test-Set Image Corruption on Fashion-MNIST

notes.problem: How robust are CNN image classifiers when only a portion of the test set is corrupted?
limitations: Only one specific corruption type (Gaussian blur + contrast enhancement) tested
Models trained only on clean data with no data augmentation or corruption-aware training
Single run results reported without statistical significance testing
notes.contribution: Empirical comparison of a custom 4-layer CNN and pretrained ResNet-18 on Fashion-MNIST under varying fractions of Gaussian blur + contrast enhancement corruption
key_findings: Custom CNN accuracy dropped from 91.31% (clean) to 10.82% at 100% corruption; ResNet-18 dropped from 88.10% to 20.44%
Entropy rose from 0.1729 to 0.5379 for the custom model and from 0.1517 to 0.3073 for ResNet-18 as corruption fraction increased
ResNet-18 was more robust, possibly due to its deeper residual structure and ImageNet pretraining preserving coarse shape information

papers.title: Evaluation of CNN Models with Fashion MNIST Data

notes.problem: Which CNN architecture performs best on the Fashion MNIST dataset?
limitations: No numerical results reported in abstract
Single dataset evaluation limits generalizability
notes.contribution: Empirical comparison of four CNN architectures on the Fashion MNIST classification task
key_findings: ResNet achieved the best classification accuracy among the four evaluated CNN models on Fashion MNIST

papers.title: An Architecture Combining Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with Batch Normalization for Apparel Image Classification
papers.venue: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Sustainable Energy, Signal Processing and Cyber Security (iSSSC)

notes.problem: How to improve accuracy and prevent overfitting in CNN-based apparel image classification
notes.contribution: A CNN architecture combining batch normalization and dropout with early stopping for apparel image classification on Fashion MNIST
key_findings: Proposed CNN models with Batch Normalization and Dropout outperform existing state-of-the-art methods in accuracy and precision on Fashion MNIST

papers.title: Improving remote sensing scene classification using quality-based data augmentation

notes.problem: How to improve CNN-based remote sensing scene classification by augmenting training data with higher-quality samples rather than randomly selected ones.
limitations: Underperformed on NWPU-RS45 in one experimental case
Online generation adds computational overhead during training
notes.contribution: A quality-based sample selection (QSS) data augmentation technique that selects the best geometrically transformed images during CNN training using prediction-probability criteria to improve remote sensing scene classification.
key_findings: QSS outperformed all previous methods on four of five datasets for both train-test splits
For 10%-90% split, QSS achieved accuracies of 94.51, 81.72, 89.89, 94.09, and 93.98 on UCMerced, Optimal31, RSSCN7, AID, and NWPU-RS45 respectively
For 20%-80% split, QSS achieved 97.09, 88.37, 94.01, 95.71, and 94.71 on the same datasets

papers.title: Transcribed Digits and Apparel Classification using Convolutional Neural Network
papers.venue: International Conference on Communication Information and Computing Technology (ICCICT)

notes.problem: How effectively can CNNs classify handwritten digits and apparel images on standard benchmark datasets?
limitations: Limited to two benchmark datasets
No comparison with other model architectures
notes.contribution: Demonstrates CNN-based image classification on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST benchmark datasets with exploration of CNN structure and hyperparameters.
key_findings: CNN models were successfully applied to both MNIST and Fashion-MNIST datasets demonstrating effectiveness for image classification tasks

papers.title: Convolutional Neural Network for Fashion Images Classification (Fashion-MNIST)
papers.venue: Journal of Applied Technology and Innovation

notes.problem: How do various parameters affect the accuracy of CNN models trained for fashion image classification?
limitations: Limited to Fashion-MNIST dataset; no comparison with other state-of-the-art models reported in abstract.
notes.contribution: A CNN-based study identifying parameters affecting accuracy for fashion image classification using the Fashion-MNIST dataset.
key_findings: Parameters such as network architecture choices affect CNN model accuracy on Fashion-MNIST classification tasks.

papers.title: LiteNet-CNN: A novel efficient lightweight image classification network
papers.venue: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Trends in Industry 4.0 Technologies (ICETI4T)

notes.problem: How to design efficient neural networks for resource-constrained environments like mobile devices with minimal parameters but strong classification performance
limitations: Evaluated only on Fashion MNIST dataset
Test accuracy of 88.66% may not be sufficient for all applications
notes.contribution: LiteNet-CNN, a lightweight CNN with only 41,610 parameters, achieving competitive image classification performance on resource-constrained devices
key_findings: LiteNet-CNN reduces trainable parameters by ~78.56% vs AlexNet and 6.34% vs LeNet, resulting in 41,610 parameters
Achieves 98.42% precision, 97.84% recall, and 88.66% test accuracy on Fashion MNIST
Training accuracy of 90.04% on Fashion MNIST

papers.title: Game Theory Meets Data Augmentation

notes.problem: How to improve data augmentation for deep learning, especially when dataset size is small.
notes.contribution: MFG Augment, a data augmentation method based on Mean-Field Game theory that synthesizes continuous paths between image distributions to generate augmented samples.
key_findings: MFG Augment achieves better generalization and higher classification accuracy than benchmark augmentation methods
MFG Augment significantly improves test accuracy when dataset size is small
MFG Augment consistently shows better affinity and diversity scores

papers.title: Deep Revamped Quantum Convolutional Neural Network on Fashion MNIST Dataset

notes.problem: Conventional neural networks suffer from overfitting and poor interpretability on low-quality images in classification tasks.

papers.title: Towards Data-Efficient Neural Network Training
